Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. has informed the Exchange that: "Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd., had been awarded the Golden Peacock Award for Excellence in Corporate Governance for the year 2006 under the "PSUs Category". The award was presented on November 29, 2006 by Honourable Chief Minister of Delhi, Smt. Sheila Dixit. The Golden Peacock award validates the Company's 'Best-in-class' Corporate Governance practices and reflects on its transparent and ethical dealings with stakeholders across the entire value chain. It recognises the Management's commitment to the highest standards of corporate conduct and its commitment to Corporate Social Responsibility as a distinct activity that helps build commendable social values and adds to the ethical fibre of the organisation. Instituted by the Institute of Directors (IOD) in 1991, the annual Golden Peacock Awards are considered the holy grail of Corporate Excellence and its guidelines provide a checklist for improvement and self-assessment in areas of quality, innovation, training, governance, environment management and corporate social responsibility. The Golden Peacock awards jury for Excellence in Corporate Governance is headed by the Former Chief Justice of India, Justice P.N. Bhagwati and comprises eminent bureaucrats and Senior Government functionaries. The winners were selected based on written submission on the Questionnaire given by Institute of Directors, which was followed by presentations by 17 shortlisted Companies including HPCL which was held on November 29, 2006 at New Delhi".

Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. has informed the Exchange that Hindusthan Petroleum Corporation Limited and G B Pant University of Agriculture & Technology Pantnagar, one of the India's premier Agriculture University have signed on January 20, 2006 a Memorandum of Understanding for Mass Cultivation of Jatropha, Installation of Biodiesel Plant and Tissue Culture Development. Biodiesel is a clean & better burning fuel which can be mixed with Diesel upto 20% and used as transport fuel without any modification in the engines. The use of Biodiesel results in substantial reduction in unburnt hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide & particulate matters. After HPCL's successful completion of field trials of Biodiesel with Brihan Mumbai Electric Supply & Transport (BEST), Mumbai, this is another step forward towards achieving new milestone. The project will be funded by HPCL & will focus on the selection of best species of Jatropha and its propagation to produce seeds of high oil content for Biodiesel production. The project will progress in a phased manner. The initial cultivation of 5 Lakhs Jatropha and installation of Biodiesel Production Unit will be undertaken in the current year 2006. The plantation of another 5 Lakhs Jatropha will be undertaken from 2007 along with Tissue Culture Research for micropropogation.
